title: Replying to @ella Accidentally went this whole video without saying W...
transcript: alright a lot of people asked me why I hate Jack Thorne and honestly I don't think I need any more reasons than Cursed Child but I have more reasons, so let's get into it so if you don't know Jack Thorne he's kind of become the go-to guy to write adaptations for popular I P especially on stage but also on TV probably nothing quite as atrocious as the scripts for Cursed Child or the King Kong musical but still a pattern of work that I think ranges from mid to bad he did the HBO adaptation of His Dark Materials which I thought really fell flat he did the screenplay for Enola Holmes which is like a feminist spin on Sherlock Holmes so I don't know why they got a man to write it but I think it really shows in the final product although I can acknowledge that I might be in the minority on that I know a lot of people like this movie on stage he did a Christmas Carol adaptation that I thought was not terrible, but not great he actually took a pretty big swing with the ending which I kind of respected but it didn't totally work for me he's also one of the writers on the Stranger Things stage play which might be the exception that proves the rule because I don't hate this script as much but he's also not the main writer on it and even still I don't think the writing is all that strong so like, how did he become the go-to guy for projects like this? and I understand writers often don't do their best work when they're taking gigs like this in order to pay the bills so that they can pursue their other artistic endeavors and likewise I get that the producers of projects like this don't want Shakespeare, they want someone who can just write a product but I don't think that's quite the issue here like a good counter-example might be someone like Anthony Mccarten who's known for writing biopics and I don't like his writing, but I get it: producers want formulaic unambitious biography screenplays and he delivers but I feel like a lot of Jack Thorne's writing skews more toward actively bad so I'm just confused how he became the Anthony Mccarten of IP adaptations and even something like Cursed Child which was very commercially successful was widely criticized for the writing so even if you're a producer who doesn't care that much about quality I still don't understand the thought process of going out of your way to be like “yes that's the guy we gotta hire again!” and maybe it is just as simple as: not everyone hates his work as much as I do which like, fair enough but that's my opinion but let me finish off this tirade by giving some credit where it's due: The movie Wonder was charming enough the stage adaptation of the vampire movie Let the Right One In was actually stunningly beautiful mostly because of John Tiffany's direction I don't remember much about Jack Thorne's script but clearly it didn't leave a negative impression on me Adolescence I haven't seen yet I know I should but I'm just kind bad at watching TV but the last thing I have to mention is the biggest plot twist in this whole saga he wrote an original play called Sunday which premiered in 2019 and I actually thought this play was quite beautiful it really struck a chord with me, especially at that age it's a play about young adults but the hilarious irony is that I was the only one who liked it everyone I knew thought it was awful including people my own age and I was like are you kidding me? the one time I go to bat for Jack Thorne and I'm completely on my own? hilarious!
